name: St. Patrick's Blue
lede: St. Patrick's Blue is a deep, near-navy blue named for the Irish patron saint, a place-and-institution color that our graph also treats as a close relative of Indigo.

sections.title: A patronal blue
sections.body: Our library files this as a place or institution name, tied to Saint Patrick and used historically as a heraldic and institutional color in Ireland, though the books we checked carry no fuller account of when or how the name was fixed to this exact navy [1]. Our graph also marks it as drawn from [[indigo]], its closest broad family, with the real nearest look-alikes being [[cosmic-cobalt]] and [[resolution-blue]], both more vivid than this deep, slightly greyed navy, and [[midnight-blue]] darker still [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this navy in 12 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.05 percent, as photographed, with the within-painting lens counting 11 — rarer than 67 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, 0.4 percent of the 1,674 paintings we have from then (6 paintings), 4.7 times the museums' expected rate, and plays an accent in 91 percent of its appearances [3]. The earliest match is Bronzino's 1543 portrait, with the latest from 1924, four dated paintings in all, too thin a sample to call it anything but a floor [3].
